The Japanese Tatewaku 立涌 pattern is a traditional motif of rising, undulating lines that swell and narrow like steam or flowing water. Its upward movement is associated with vitality, growth, prosperity, and the continuous flow of good fortune. Because the lines rise without breaking, Tatewaku also suggests energy, longevity, and an auspicious path toward the future. The elegant rhythm of the waves has made Tatewaku a cherished motif in kimono, textiles, and other forms of Japanese decorative art.
